angles.drive: Every duty offered gets a yes before you check its cost. Since being counted on is where your standing lives, you never say no to the next request ahead of finishing the last. You pay for your standing in the strength that keeps it.
angles.cost_self: Whenever you say yes, you spend hours promised to yourself. Because holding things together comes ahead of getting home, you trade sleep for another duty. By the end of most weeks, you are short of sleep and of the strength to say yes.
angles.cost_others: Saying yes to everyone keeps your place in their lives. Because a refusal feels like lost standing, you give everyone a slice rather than anyone your whole self. You save the thinnest slice for those who need you most.

renames.why: Never says no is the Artisan's keyword (Wood, Fire).

angles.drive: Keeping your word matters more than being liked. You carry a promise like a debt until paid, so your word gets kept ahead of your way out. A handshake with you is as good as a contract.
angles.cost_self: Changing your mind is harder than keeping your word. Your word stays kept past its reason rather than broken, since breaking it dents how steady you feel. Being someone whose yes never moves is what you need underneath.
angles.cost_others: Where your word is kept, you expect it back. You hold the person you love to a word given in another mood rather than let it go. Old promises stay binding on both of you, long after the mood that made them.

renames.why: Keeps your word is the Magistrate's keyword (Wood, Metal).

angles.drive: You sleep on a question rather than answer on the spot. Forcing an answer now feels like lying to you, and you give the question a night first. Your decisions come late and hold up for years.
angles.cost_self: Sleeping on a question makes the answer real. Being sure later matters more to you than being in it now, so the opening that wanted an answer closes. Some good chances go to quicker people while you are still deciding.
angles.cost_others: With an answer someone needs, you sleep on it before you give it. Sleeping on it matters more than a quick reply, and you leave whoever asked waiting longer. What they get from you in the end is a word you will stand by.

renames.why: Sleeps on it is the Steward's keyword (Water).

angles.drive: Giving freely is what you do first with what comes in. You feel money belongs to whoever needs it next, and you give it on rather than set it aside. Friends in a tight month find your hand already open.
angles.cost_self: Keeping is harder for you than giving freely. You would rather give money on than sit with it, since holding still feels like being stuck. Your own hard year finds the account empty.
angles.cost_others: With the people around you, giving freely is how you stay close. You give to the newest friend more freely than to the oldest one, since newness is what moves you. Your household lives on whatever is left over.

renames.why: Gives freely is the Artisan's keyword (Fire).

angles.drive: Playing it safe is a choice you make before looking at the others. You carry Earth past what you need, so you play safe to be held instead of tested. You rest in the safe place rather than live in it.
angles.cost_self: Most days you play safe without noticing you chose. Because you fear the unknown more than you mind being bored, you pick the safe one and call the boredom peace. You buy that peace with the chances you turn down untried.
angles.cost_others: Handed someone's plan to change the shared life, you play safe for both. Keeping things as they are matters more than any change, and you slow it down. You take away their equal say in the life you share.

renames.why: Plays it safe is the Steward's keyword (Fire, Metal). Write it to the owner's reading of the Sage: drawn to shelter, or shelter comes to them.

angles.drive: You play safe before you know the odds. Keeping what you have feels more like you than reaching, so you take the safe way ahead of the good one. You pay for playing it safe in chances you never took.
angles.cost_self: Playing safe keeps the floor under you. Because a wrong move costs you more than a missed one, you keep playing it safe with the job you have. You let every chance you play safe around close, and the work you wanted goes with it.
angles.cost_others: For everyone waiting on your yes, you play it safe too. You would rather give a safe no than a yes that can fail. You put their plans on hold for as long as you hesitate.

renames.why: Plays it safe is the Steward's keyword. Owner-approved new word: "Holds the yes" (use it).

angles.drive: You shut people out before they get close enough to press on you. Since your own pressure is plenty, shutting out anyone else's feels like safety rather than loss. You lose the closeness along with the pressure you keep out.
angles.cost_self: Where help is offered, you shut it out kindly. You want no one pressing on you more than anyone helping, and what was meant for two gets carried by one. You end up paying alone for every hand you turned away.
angles.cost_others: Reaching for you is pressure too, and you shut out the people who try. You would rather be alone than understood, and the door shuts hardest on those closest. You leave them outside with no reason and no way to ask for one.

renames.why: Shuts people out is the Twin's keyword (Earth). The General drifted into the Twin's withdrawal here; write the General (takes charge, hard on yourself, never off duty).

angles.drive: What you make is made to last, slowly and on purpose. The making itself is the enjoyment, so you make things for the years rather than for the showing. Your work is still in daily use long after the fashion has moved on.
angles.cost_self: Making things last is your idea of doing something right. Since the work is only right once it holds, you would rather be finished than first. Rougher versions reach people before yours do, and the praise goes with them.
angles.cost_others: You make things last for your family rather than arrive on time. You never count the waiting, and next year you deliver what was needed this year. They manage without for a year while your careful version takes shape.

renames.why: Makes things last is the Steward's keyword (Earth). The auditor proposed "Unhurried" for the Artisan, the one who enjoys the making.

angles.drive: Being hard to reach is where you rest. You hold more Water than you show, so you keep your warmth out of reach rather than let anyone feel it. Keep in mind that you want someone to reach you all the same.
angles.cost_self: Out of reach is where your depths feel safe. More Water sits in you than you move, so you would rather be useful than known. You give up closeness each time you stay out of reach, and it rarely comes back on its own.
angles.cost_others: Staying hard to reach leaves the people who love you guessing. You keep closeness in reserve rather than spend it, and they get your help in place of your company. You make the people closest to you do all the reaching.

renames.why: Hard to reach is the Alchemist's keyword (Earth, Metal, Water).

angles.drive: A finished thing gives you a calm that starting never does. Since a half-done piece sits with you like an open promise, you finish one thing properly rather than start three. The things you make arrive whole, every edge seen to.
angles.cost_self: Finishing comes before enjoying for you. A thing is not yours to like until it is done, and you finish the gift ahead of the pleasure of making it. The best part of the work goes by while your mind waits for the end.
angles.cost_others: Every gift you give, you finish alone. The making feels like part of you, so you finish it yourself rather than with the person it is for. The one it is for gets your polish and misses the hours behind it.

renames.why: Finishes things is the Steward's keyword (Metal). The Artisan on Metal had drifted into a perfectionist; write the Artisan (makes and gives with ease and enjoyment).

angles.drive: You love people by correcting them. Getting someone right feels like caring to you, so you fix the small wrong thing rather than sit with the whole sad one. Remember that you are allowed to sit with a sad thing and fix nothing.
angles.cost_self: Loving by correcting costs you the ones who stop bringing things. You put being useful to someone ahead of being close to them, and the corrected learn to bring you only finished things. You get respect for it, and the closeness goes somewhere less exact.
angles.cost_others: Correcting is what you give people wanting comfort. You would rather set people straight than let them be, and you send them home taught instead of held. With every correction, you take from them the comfort they came for.

renames.why: "Loves by correcting" is neither side of the Sage. Owner-approved new word "Waits to be told" with an approved drive (in approved_drive); write cost_self and cost_others to match.
renames.approved_drive: You wait to be told before you trust your own read. A word from someone wiser feels like cover, and you keep asking long after you know. You hand your best judgement to people who know less than you do.

texts.text: Whenever someone arrives to be held, you steady them instead. A standard feels more useful to you than a kind word, and you hand the one who came for comfort a lesson. Your warmth reaches them a step behind your advice.
texts.why: The Sage on Metal turns into a corrector here ("hand the one who came for comfort a lesson"). Rewrite the first two sentences to the owner's reading of the Sage; the close (from M1) may stay if it still fits.

texts.text: You over-protect the people you love from what they could survive. Watching someone struggle hurts you more than doing it for them, so the help comes before the asking. Remember that you love them just as much when you let them struggle.
texts.why: This page also shows "Lets it drift" and "Stays sheltered". Link them as the owner approved for the Fire Sage: protecting others is the outer act of someone who wants shelter. Change only the middle sentence, e.g. "Feeling safe is what you want most, and you shelter them the way you wish to be sheltered." The friction close may stay.
